summary: A fiction excerpt (apparently from a Cory Doctorow-style novel, though the author isn't named) in which Mr Gonzales, a venture capital franchisee, pitches funding to Diana, a 60-year-old engineer in Calvinia who turns shipping-container junk into new products using 3D printing and evolutionary design. She rejects his $300,000 minimum angel round, arguing she can grow organically and that his gigafund's structure can't deploy capital efficiently.
one_line: In a fiction excerpt, a sixty-year-old Calvinia engineer who recycles container junk into printed products rebuffs a gigafund VC's oversized investment offer.
key_facts: After the WTO, the Chinese spent 25 years brute-forcing the problem-space of all possible 3D plastic objects that an American might pay money for.
Much of that plastic stuff sits on container ships in international waters, waiting for someone to pay the carbon taxes to land it.
Diana is an engineer living in Calvinia who imports junk electronics, chassis and parts and prints the actuators, controllers and wires herself.
Her design process: tumble parts to scan them, run an evolutionary algorithm to fit them together, and cull the ugly mutants while cultivating the pretty ones.
Diana can produce fifty original designs in a day and uses more than 80 percent of any container's payload; the rest goes to feedstockers to be eaten by bacteria.
She says manufacturing is easy 'monkey labor' because every kid, especially girls, takes shop class nowadays.
She made sub-micro solar cars for her parents' anniversary, saying no one wants to drive a truck anymore.
To double her operation she would need about 60 grand, and Gonzales's franchise's smallest angel round is three hundred kay ($300,000).
Gonzales offers to roll her round up with five or six similar firms; Diana says this would increase her communications and bureaucracy overhead by 3,000 percent.
Diana is growing organically, putting her best contractors on the payroll, and says at sixty she doesn't need to 'grow like a tumor anymore.'
Diana can turn 60 grand into 600 in six months, but says she can't turn a million into ten million in six years.
Gonzales's franchise is a gigafund (a billion dollars), and Diana points out it will still be sitting on three quarters of it by the time the fund cashes out when investing in $300,000 increments.
